main_text.p: Hinc concludunt, non veram, sed Metaphoricam esse hanc nostram Redemtionem.

1. Quoniam in ea[?] nemo fit, qui pretium accipiat. Si enim id, quod in ipsa pretii loco est, acceptum (ab eo scilicet, qui captivum hominem detinebat) fuisset: iam non metaphoricum, sed verum pretium intervenisset, uti inquiunt.

2. Quoniam Redimendi verbum, non-aliquando, non etiam saepe, sed plerumque & fere semper apud sacros Scriptores metaphoricam prorsus significationem obtineat, adeo ut nihil aliud sit Redimere, quam liberare, aut sibi afferere, quamvis veri pretii verasolutio aliquando non interveniat.

1. Sicut dicitur in Veteri Testamento Deus Redemisse populum Israeliticum, quem ex Ægyptiorum, & Pharaonis servitute liberaverat, & sibi quodammodo afferverat, quamvis nullum pretium pro eo liberando solvisset. 2. Sicut Moses a Stephano Actor, 7. λυτρωτὴς sive Redemtor est appel-latus.

page.notes: The first line of the page has a fragment before "Hinc"; I treated it as continuing the previous page. The word "ea" in paragraph 1 is uncertain (the scan is smudged), so it is marked [?]. The Greek word λυτρωτὴς is partly faint and may need checking. The "2." in the last paragraph is an inline number within the same paragraph. A small mark at the top left, beside the running head, is not printed text and was left out. "afferverat" follows the u/v rule for the printed "afferuerat".
